2607.29561.title: MOT-SR: Multi-Objective Tool-Augmented Scientific Equation Discovery with Large Language Models
2607.29561.paper_summary: Symbolic Regression (SR) aims to discover analytical equations from observational data and plays a central role in scientific modeling. While recent Large Language Model (LLM) based approaches show promise, they face two limitations. First, they lack data analysis mechanisms for uncovering variable dependencies, which reduces the efficiency of equation discovery. Second, most methods rely on single-objective evaluation focused solely on fitting error. This neglect of structural complexity and generalization often causes models to converge prematurely to local optima, limiting their ability to explore the broader equation space. We propose Multi-Objective Tool-augmented Symbolic Regression (MOT-SR), a unified framework that integrates external analytical tools to extract structural priors and guide equation generation, while jointly optimizing for accuracy, complexity, and generalization via a multi-objective evaluation module that maintains a dynamic Pareto front. MOT-SR employs two collaborative LLM modules: a Meta Strategy Generator, which selects tools and synthesizes structural optimization strategies based on Pareto-optimal equations, and an Equation Generator, which produces new candidate equations accordingly. The system operates in a closed-loop manner, continuously refining both strategies and equation structures. Across 40 standard tasks, MOT-SR outperforms existing SR methods in accuracy, generalization, and efficiency. We further validate MOT-SR on extreme mass-ratio inspiral (EMRI) orbital modeling, an important problem in space-based gravitational-wave astronomy where small local errors can accumulate substantially over long-term evolution. The discovered interpretable correction achieves the lowest trajectory-level integration error on held-out configurations. These results demonstrate the potential of MOT-SR to enable reliable modeling of long-horizon scientific dynamics.
2607.29561.paper_summary_zh: 符號回歸（SR）旨在從觀察數據中發現分析方程，並在科學建模中扮演核心角色。<lb/>雖然最近基於大型語言模型（LLM）的方法顯示出潛力，但它們面臨兩個限制。<lb/>首先，它們缺乏數據分析機制來揭示變量依賴性，這降低了方程發現的效率。<lb/>其次，大多數方法依賴於僅專注於擬合誤差的單一目標評估。<lb/>這種對結構複雜性和泛化的忽視，常常導致模型過早收斂到局部最優，限制了它們探索更廣泛方程空間的能力。<lb/>我們提出了多目標工具增強符號回歸（MOT-SR），這是一個統一框架，整合外部分析工具以提取結構先驗並指導方程生成，同時通過一個保持動態帕累托前沿的多目標評估模塊聯合優化準確性、複雜性和泛化。<lb/>MOT-SR 採用兩個協作的 LLM 模塊：一個元策略生成器，根據帕累托最優方程選擇工具並綜合結構優化策略；一個方程生成器，根據需要生成新的候選方程。<lb/>該系統以閉環方式運作，持續完善策略和方程結構。<lb/>在 40 個標準任務中，MOT-SR 在準確性、泛化和效率上超越了現有的 SR 方法。<lb/>我們進一步在極端質量比啟發（EMRI）軌道建模上驗證了 MOT-SR，這是一個在基於太空的引力波天文學中重要的問題，其中小的局部誤差在長期演化中可以顯著累積。<lb/>所發現的可解釋修正在保留配置上達到了最低的軌跡級整合誤差。<lb/>這些結果展示了 MOT-SR 在可靠建模長期科學動力學方面的潛力。
